title: Lessons from MRT Service Disruptions in February 2025 and Actions to Prevent Similar Breakdowns
what_it_is: Lessons from MRT Service Disruptions in February 2025 and Actions to Prevent Similar Breakdowns

sections.label: February 2025 MRT disruptions questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Transport for updates on lessons learnt from February 2025 MRT disruptions and actions to prevent repeats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether an update can be provided on the lessons learnt from the recent MRT service disruptions on the North-South Line on 7 February 2025, North-East Line on 10 February 2025 and Circle Line on 11 February 2025; and (b) what are the actions that the Ministry will take to prevent a repeat of similar breakdowns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether any of the recent MRT disruptions leading to delays in MRT services on the North-South Line, North-East Line and Circle Line in February 2025 were caused by a maintenance issues; and (b) what steps will be taken to ensure that similar incidents can be minimised or avoided in future.

sections.label: Trains launched before vehicle stalled
sections.summary: When the engineering vehicle stalled, only three of 39 scheduled NSL trains had been launched from Bishan Depot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: By the time the engineering vehicle stalled, only three out of 39 trains that were scheduled to serve the NSL that morning had been launched from Bishan Depot.

sections.label: SMRT restored NSL and EWL service
sections.summary: After safety checks, SMRT launched trains from Bishan Depot from 6.36 pm and progressively restored normal NSL and EWL service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: After completing a series of thorough checks to ensure safety, SMRT was able to launch trains from Bishan Depot from 6.36 pm and progressively restored normal train service for commuters on the NSL and EWL.

sections.label: Three February incidents unrelated
sections.summary: Preliminary findings show the three incidents were unrelated, involved different lines, components and teams, and did not cause prolonged stoppage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Our preliminary findings show that the three incidents were unrelated – they involve different lines, different components, and different operations and maintenance teams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Unlike some previous disruptions where trains were unable to continue travelling on the tracks, the three incidents did not result in a prolonged stoppage of train services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Trains could continue to run along the NSL, NEL and CCL, albeit at longer intervals or slower speeds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: However, as these incidents happened during the morning peak hours, they affected a larger number of commuters and lengthened the waiting and travel times.

sections.label: MRT network MKBF target achieved
sections.summary: As at 25 February 2025, MRT network MKBF is about two million train-kilometres and all lines met the one million target.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As at 25 February 2025, the MKBF for our MRT network stands at about two million train-kilometres and all MRT lines have achieved our target MKBF of at least one million train-kilometres.

sections.label: LTA probing MRT disruption causes
sections.summary: On 13 February, LTA announced it was looking into the root causes of MRT disruptions after three incidents in a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On 13 February, LTA announced that it was looking into the root causes of MRT disruptions after three incidents in a week.

sections.label: EWL investigation findings and incidents
sections.summary: Findings of the EWL investigation will be shared publicly, and three unrelated incidents do not show a systemic issue requiring a Committee of Inquiry.

sentences.text: When the investigation for the EWL is completed, we will share the findings publicly, so that we learn from what happened and how we can do better.

And because these three incidents, even though they happened in quick succession, they are unrelated to one another and also to the EWL incident, there is not a systemic issue or concern with SBST or SMRT that I think will change our position on the necessity for a Committee of Inquiry.

sections.label: Rescue train and derailed vehicle
sections.summary: A rescue train was sent to push the stalled engineering vehicle, but its wheels came off the rails and heavy lifting equipment could not be deployed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, the first thing that they did was to send a rescue train – and this is part of the standard operating procedure – to try and push the stalled engineering vehicle so that they are able to move it and clear the tracks for the trains to be launched from Bishan Depot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But unfortunately, in the process of doing so, they discovered that the wheels of the engineering vehicle came off the rails.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, they were unable to continue pushing and they had to use a different method.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And because of the space constraints, they were unable to deploy heavy lifting equipment at this location.

sections.label: Investing in worker upskilling
sections.summary: The government will continue to invest in upskilling workers and giving them access to good technologies and a good working environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Minister Chee, I hope your answer will be succinct as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We will continue to invest in this area to upskill our workers and to make sure that they are able to have access to good technologies and a good working environment.
